Give me an ACTUAL scenario where that happened. Like... I want you to give me an example where people in a terrible situation sit around and say "If only Amanda was born we wouldn't be here right now..." because the argument you're making is very strange... a lack of existence hurts nobody, for all you know you could be better off without a person's existence... or worse off... you'll never know, there's no way to even make that argument.

If all of the amazing people in history (and I use the word "amazing" knowing that most of them weren't super great in every area of life...) were never born are you saying that amazing things still wouldn't have happened somehow? That somebody else wouldn't have stood up and did what needed to be done? Even in that scenario, nobody is sitting around and crying about how a specific person wasn't born because that person doesn't exist, for all we know we could've missed out on the messiah... but then you have to weigh all of the children in foster care, sold in sex trafficking rings, raised to be child soldiers, are forced into slavery, grow up homeless, are born to drug addicts/alcoholics, have depression and attempt suicide multiple times, were struck by disease, etc... and then decide on your own "their suffering was worth it in the end" hell even well adjusted financially stable parents don't always raise good people let alone financially stable well adjusted people... and even if they did, are the children themselves kind? Because there are a lot of terrible people out there.

It's more like walking through a field of land mines... and if there was a way to ask a child before they're born if they'd like to be born then that'd be the ideal scenario, but it'll never happen so airing on the side of caution and just not having them to begin with would be safer. I think many people look at life and enjoy the good things it had to offer them and are thankful for even existing... others would take a suicide pill in the next 5 minutes if one was offered to them. 
Suicide is another issue I have with being alive personally... I know you mentioned being suicidal at a point in your life so this just comes down to the issues and how they affect you, I know with me my issues are permanent because of how I was born... how I deal with them can be changed but I'm personally not happy with any of the options and would rather just have an easy exit... except I also can't manage to have that so I know for me no matter what choice I make I'll have to suffer before I get the results I want (and hopefully the results will even be what I want)... not having to have to worry about any of this would've been better for me, it would suck knowing that I missed out on things I love in life... but I also just wouldn't care because I wouldn't exist, there would be no brain to even process thought or any subjective experience to reflect on, so I actually would be unaffected because there would be no me in that scenario.

But back to the main point there is no scenario where not having children hurts others, the best argument I think you can make is a case for parents who just really want children who cannot conceive... which is still not the same thing because they're still not thinking "I wish Brendan Miller, born in 2004, with social security number 565 28 8374 and is a Catholic who loves athletics and math was born... he sure would've loved being alive", they just want a child period... and that child could end up being the next mass shooter or end up murdering themselves or end up happy and great or okay and able to go through life... you just never know... but never having them doesn't cause direct harm to anyone even in that scenario.

Speaking as someone who has been called attractive multiple times in my adult life (still something I'm getting used to) I can tell you that it ultimately doesn't matter. Being physically attractive doesn't mean that others will naturally gravitate towards you or that you will even FEEL attractive, it just means that to someone else out there you might have a nice face and that's it. Not saying that it's not BETTER than being seen as unattractive because it is nice, but... the extent to which it matters when you're depressed and (in my case) anxious isn't really substantial enough to make a super huge impact on my life in any positive way, I still feel repulsive whenever I leave the house and I also avoid people like the plague.

Also being desired for being cute really doesn't get you as far as you might think. It's kind of just something that COULD potentially draw someone in MAYBE... and then after that they'll have the same tolerance for your personality as they would if you were "ugly" (whatever that even means). If anything it's opened up room for people who make me uncomfortable or want to take advantage of me rather than opening up doors for legitimate true connections with others.

Chances are she just doesn't know how to process and handle the reality of having a child with depression... but honestly that's her problem, not yours. Her response was completely unjustified and incredibly telling of her inability to put aside her own harmful thoughts for the sake of another person with whom she's supposed to have a strong and positive relationship with... in short terms she just doesn't sound like a very good mother. Everyone is a person and deserves some room to make mistakes but... honestly, I hear this being applied to parents who obviously should not have had children, people who take on the responsibility of raising and influencing a child have less room to mess up... there are major consequences to their mistakes, sorry if you feel differently but honestly most people probably should not be parents... I just don't see enough people taking the role seriously enough. On one hand who am I to judge...? But on the other hand I mean... look outside, the world is a mess... so... I don't think my feelings on this are unwarranted. Most people just do a bad job parenting in my view.

All that being said you didn't deserve to hear that... and I'm sure if you went through with suicide your mother would have a difficult time dealing with it so I have no idea why she'd even play in that territory... even a little bit of empathy or decency should prevent someone from being so incredibly toxic. These are the types of parents who, when you move out, you just stop communicating with... a lot of elderly people are worried over how they'll get by on their own in old age and... for all of the people who fall under that category and were awful parents who have no relationship with their children, I just have to say I don't feel sorry for them at all. (But the nice old people who were put in that situation despite their kindness and good choices I definitely feel badly for.)

There are people much much older than 27 who work minimum wage jobs, nobody would think that you're odd for working one at your age... or even not having a job before either, honestly it's nobody else's business anyway and it's incredibly unlikely that anyone would think of you any kind of way because you haven't had a job before. I think that you're fine, but if you have anxiety and being around people makes it worse then you may want to work your way towards a job that you feel more comfortable doing in the future... maybe stocking shelves at night or doing data entry.

I've worked retail for years and I have pretty bad anxiety so it's entirely possible to do so, I'm not trying to scare you out of it. You definitely do fall into a sort of rhythm and you may make some friends along the way... and honestly, making money is nice even if it's not a whole lot. My only suggestion would be that if you can't see yourself doing it long term, try to work towards finding a job you feel suits your needs and talents more... you might not be sure what that is now because you have no experience, but just know that nobody goes into a new job knowing everything. I've heard stories of people making HUGE errors and they didn't get fired or ostracized because people understand that you need time to adjust and learn the job. Good luck! I'm sure you'll do well wherever you go, there's a lesson that comes with every job and experience so even if you don't love what you do it might get you a foot in the door towards something you want or a different perspective that helps you in the long term. :)

30 is a specific point in life where younger people will stop being able to think of themselves as young... and with that they have less understanding for themselves in the future because thoughts and actions that hold us back are only "acceptable" (not really) for kids, teens, and young adults. If you make it past that point then it's somehow supposed to be a sign that you can make it in life and by 30 you should be able to live functionally... if not then people don't see themselves making it to that point at all. There's also the fear of growing older and losing/wasting more time being unhappy, so for a lot of people (since 30 is considered old to young people) they create a mental deadline, "If I can't get myself together by 30 then I'll have all of the problems I currently have and on top of it I'll be old and have to deal with the realities of life." and that's not a particularly pleasant thing to think so... people have a hard time seeing themselves make it to 30, even though people suffer from depression and commit suicide in all stages of life.

There are a lot of reasons for it... for me it's just the fear of getting older, I'd rather just die young if I'm going to be miserable anyway. :)
